title: Caral
summary: Caral is an archaeological site in Peru's Supe Valley, north of Lima and inland from the Pacific coast. It has large pyramid mounds, the biggest called the Pirámide Mayor. Sources place its occupation from about 2900 BCE and its main construction around 2600 BCE; the cause of its abandonment is unknown.

uncertainty.note: Sources give different spans (c. 3000–1800 BCE, 2900–1600 BCE, construction c. 2600 BCE); the record uses the EBSCO span of first occupation (2900 BCE) to abandonment (about 1600 BCE).

as_recorded.value: constructed around 2600 B.C., roughly the same time as the earliest Egyptian pyramid
may have been inhabited as far back as 2900 B.C.E.; abandoned about 1600 B.C.E.

where.historical_name: Caral in the Supe Valley, central coastal Peru; no polity name is given in the sources

importance.justification: History.com places its building around the time of the earliest Egyptian pyramid, making it among the oldest monumental centres in the Americas.

sources.title: Caral, Peru: Norte Chico, oldest civilization in the Western Hemisphere

reviewer_note: Dates conflict across sources (see when.uncertainty). No model: heights found for the Pirámide Mayor conflict (18 m EBSCO; "nearly 100 feet" History.com) and no UNESCO or heritage-body page could be opened (UNESCO returned 403), so no sourced height plus plan dimension.
